counselFlags: Sealing is not expungement: North Dakota usually offers sealing or closing, not broad expungement. Sealing limits disclosure of court and prosecution records; it may not delete records or remove records held by BCI, law enforcement, federal systems, private background-check companies, or licensing agencies.

Agency scope: Chapter 12-60.1 sealing does not reach BCI criminal history record information or Criminal Justice Data Information Sharing System data; federal, tribal, out-of-state, and private background-check records are not cleared by North Dakota sealing.

Route scope: North Dakota court sealing reaches court and prosecution records only; federal, tribal, out-of-state, BCI criminal-history, and private background-check records are not cleared by North Dakota sealing.

Eligibility: Conviction sealing under N.D.C.C. § 12-60.1-02: a misdemeanor conviction (guilty plea or finding) may be sealed with no new conviction for at least 3 years before filing; a felony conviction with no new conviction for at least 5 years before filing; and an unconditional gubernatorial pardon can support a sealing petition.

Court findings: For a conviction-sealing petition the petitioner must prove, by clear and convincing evidence, good cause, that the benefit to the petitioner outweighs the presumption of openness, completion of all imprisonment and probation, payment of all restitution, and that reformation/rehabilitation warrants relief.

Burden and timing: The court may hold a hearing no earlier than 45 days after filing; the petitioner must prove the sealing factors by clear and convincing evidence. If denied, the court may prohibit refiling for up to one year for good cause.

Excluded offences: Offenses requiring registration under N.D.C.C. § 12.1-32-15 (including offenders against children and sexual offenders) are barred from Chapter 12-60.1 sealing. Certain felony offenses involving violence or intimidation during the firearm-disability period are excluded from Chapter 12-60.1 sealing. DUI records are excluded from Chapter 12-60.1 and use the separate § 39-08-01.6 pathway; commercial drivers are excluded from DUI sealing, and prosecutors may still access prior DUI records for enhancement purposes.

filing.feeWaiverRule: No fee amount is stated by any committed North Dakota source for a Chapter 12-60.1 petition, so this packet states none and offers no fee-waiver application. filing.hearingRule: A sealing hearing under Chapter 12-60.1 may not be held earlier than 45 days after the petition is filed, unless the prosecutor stipulates to sealing without a hearing or on a faster schedule.
filing.orderOfOperations: Serve the petition and proposed order on the prosecuting attorney; the prosecutor is expected, to the extent practicable, to notify and seek input from law enforcement, witnesses, victims, and correctional authorities.
filing.petitionContentsRule: The petition must include the petitioner's full name and all aliases, address history from the offense date to the petition date, reasons sealing should be granted, complete criminal history (North Dakota, other states, federal court, and foreign countries), all prior and pending charges, all deferred/stayed/continued-for-dismissal matters, and any prior pardon, expungement, sealing, or return-of-arrest-record requests.
filing.scopeRule: North Dakota court sealing reaches court and prosecution records only; federal, tribal, out-of-state, BCI criminal-history, and private background-check records are not cleared by North Dakota sealing.
filing.venue: The existing criminal case for the offence, under N.D.C.C. § 12-60.1-03(1). There is no separate civil action. District court or municipal court, whichever holds the case.

filingRequirementBasis: N.D.C.C. § 12-60.1-03: the participant serves the prosecuting attorney and files a petition, a mandatory proposed order and a proof of service with the clerk of the existing criminal case. No relief occurs unless the participant files.
